static_traits.name: Zhou Cheng
static_traits.social_status: Has a support network of a spouse and close friends, but shares guilt and self-blame feelings less out of fear of being judged; interpersonal relationships strained by self-blame
static_traits.medical_history: Uses a wheelchair for mobility; no other major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, with good logic and high cooperativeness, can describe automatic thoughts and bodily reactions; tends toward overthinking and self-blame, and self-reproaching sentence patterns of 'I should ...' appear in the speech

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel others are blaming me, even when there is no evidence; this leads to guilt and self-blame. The problem has been more intense over the past few months, appearing almost daily, especially obvious when things go wrong after interacting with people.
basic_info.core_demands: This guilt and self-blame are affecting my relationships and emotional health; I want to work through and overcome these patterns; I really want to find a way to stop this constant feeling of guilt.
growth_experiences: During the growth process, family members often criticized the client; when things went wrong, even if only indirectly, it was often attributed to the client. Long being in an atmosphere of criticism and blame made them gradually internalize a tendency to blame themselves first when encountering problems and take on too much responsibility.

special_situations.event: When project timelines at work have problems and responsibility has not yet been discussed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Whenever an error occurs, others will pin the responsibility on me; I must apologize and fix it immediately to avoid worse evaluations
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Apologizes preemptively, works overtime quickly to repair, takes responsibility proactively

special_situations.event: When problems arise on a family outing due to arrangements or weather not going smoothly (the trip proposed by myself)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a plan I proposed is not perfect or something unexpected happens, it is my fault; a good partner / family member should foresee and avoid all problems
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly apologizes and self-blames, over-explains, and avoids making suggestions afterward
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone must think I messed it up; I should have known better how to avoid this situation.

special_situations.event: When the team does not reach its goal (e.g. 'we did not win')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Team failure means I fail and must bear the main responsibility, otherwise others will blame me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attributes failure to oneself, doubles efforts to compensate and prevent being blamed
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: We did not win; they must blame me.

special_situations.event: In social situations, once any small mistake appears, the people around stay silent or have not yet stated their position clearly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Silence equals dissatisfaction or blame; only apologizing first can maintain relationship safety
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Apologizing immediately; nervously withdrawing; reducing expression to avoid being judged again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are disappointed in me; they must be blaming me in their hearts.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and accepted, no longer blamed; hoping for safety and affirmation in relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being blamed, judged, and rejected; worrying about being negated for failing
defense_goal: Soothes others and avoids conflict and being attacked through preemptive self-blame and apology
Withdrawing and avoiding to reduce the risk of being judged
Attributes responsibility internally to maintain a sense of control over the situation

object_relations.self_representation: A person at fault who needs to take responsibility for the problem
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh others who are always ready to place responsibility on me (family/colleagues)

object_relations.self_representation: A person who disappoints the partner and adds burden
object_relations.object_representation: A partner dissatisfied with oneself, easily dragged down by oneself

manifestations: Afraid of being judged and not daring to share real distress with spouse and close friends
Feeling isolated and blamed when others are silent or things go wrong

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worried about being judged, reduces help-seeking from significant others
Immediately contracts boundaries and becomes overly cautious when interaction goes wrong

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Assuming others blame oneself when there is no evidence (mind-reading attribution)
Projecting the inner self-blame experience as others' dissatisfaction or negation

positive_force: Has a support network of a spouse and close friends
Willing to seek help and cooperate with treatment, with clear motivation
Having some self-observation ability (able to record and identify automatic thoughts and bodily reactions)
Able to accept and try new cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments
negative_force: A long-internalized pattern of self-blame and taking responsibility (stemming from family experiences of criticism and blame)
Cognitive distortions such as mind reading, over-attribution, catastrophizing, and 'should' statements
Fears being judged, leading to avoidance of sharing and seeking support
Excessive apologizing and withdrawing reinforcing anxiety and guilt, maintaining the problem cycle
Persistent guilt affects work performance and self-care

target_behavior.behavior: Immediately self-blaming and excessively apologizing/withdrawing when problems arise in front of others, accompanied by significant anxiety reactions (racing heartbeat, stomach tightening)
antecedent: Project timelines going wrong at work
Family activities not going smoothly (suggestions made by oneself)
The team not yet reaching its goal
Small mistakes in social interactions or others' silence not yet stating their position
target_behavior.core_reason: Being frequently criticized and indirectly blamed in the family early on, forming the core beliefs 'It is all my fault' / 'I will be blamed', maintained in reality through cognitive biases like mind reading, personalization, and 'should' phrasing
target_behavior.function: Escaping criticism and conflict; seeking others' approval and relationship security; gaining short-term anxiety relief and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension; work performance affected; daily self-care declining; guilt and anxiety maintained over the long term
